subject: Day 30: one month; firm up the help network
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 30. One month. Feeding cadence is steady, social smiles are appearing more reliably, and head control is visibly stronger. With the harder weeks ahead, this is the right day to firm up the help network rather than improvise it later.

Action items
- List the two or three people you can call at 2am for an extra set of hands — a relative, a postpartum doula, a close friend. Confirm each is willing and reachable.
- Write the evening-rotation plan on the fridge so it is not renegotiated at the moment of need.
- Verify Avi is on the health-insurance plan and the member number is accessible from your phone. Healthcare.gov on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is scheduled. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Evening cluster fussiness; hiccups during or after feeds; a quiet startle to loud sounds.
- [low concern] Brief head lifts during tummy time; social smiles consolidating.
- [monitor] Caregiver burnout signals — a short fuse, dread of the evenings, persistent low mood — name them out loud before the worst night.
- [call within 24h] Sustained feeding refusal; forceful projectile vomiting; fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Read aloud 15 minutes a day; aim toward the 1,000-books-before-kindergarten frame — about one book a day from now gets you there. Reach Out and Read evidence base: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Plan a low-stimulation SF outing for a calm morning — an early stroller loop through the SF Botanical Garden or the California Academy of Sciences before crowds build. California Academy of Sciences: https://www.calacademy.org/
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day across multiple bouts; a baby-safe mirror at eye level motivates head lifts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take conversational turns with each vocalization during alert windows. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: peak crying.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
